title: The optimal sorting network on 3 channels has exactly 3 comparators
statement: S(3) = 3: some comparator network of 3 comparators sorts every input of length 3, and no network of 2 comparators does.

evidence.supports: no network of 2 comparators sorts all 3-input sequences
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-cnf --example sorting_network -- --n 3 --size 2 --sym full 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '(Unsat|Sat)')" = Unsat
evidence.notes: Optimality-as-UNSAT: no optimizer and no MaxSAT is involved. The verdict is reproduced under every symmetry setting including `--sym none`, which is the control that matters -- an UNSOUND symmetry break manufactures a wrong UNSAT, and would show as Unsat under `full` but Sat under `none`.

evidence.supports: an explicit 3-comparator network sorts every input
evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-cnf --example sorting_network -- --n 3 --size 3 --sym full 2>/dev/null | grep -q SORTS
evidence.notes: The witness network is replayed over all 2^3 zero-one inputs by a checker that shares no code with the SAT search. The 0-1 principle makes that sufficient for all totally ordered inputs.

provenance.established_by: axeyum SAT core, both bounds; symmetry-breaking soundness controlled
provenance.source: lane `sorting-networks` (terminated on an API spend limit); completed by the coordinator

prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source

notes: A new domain for the ledger: algorithms. Deliberately started at values the literature already knows, so the encoder is validated against ground truth before any frontier claim. n=6 is NOT here: size 10 refutes in 37 s but size 11 exceeds ten minutes on this encoder, so S(6) >= 11 is all that is established locally and the run was moved to an idle host.
